transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Alicia (Brightleaf), Devon (Brightleaf SRE), Tom (Brightleaf Product)
Links shared: poc playbook (short): https://redwood.ai/poc-playbook (sent after the call), benchmark spreadsheet: (link posted in chat).

Summary: quick progress check on onboarding, creds and infra readiness; triage of two latency anomalies in staging; agree next steps for canary run and quant profile tests; confirm security docs handoff timeline.

Topics: onboarding progress, staging network + CIDR, KMS/SAML handoff, quantization tests, fallback/canary plan, SLA expectations.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: okay, hi everyone, thanks for jumping on. we have about 40 minutes, we want to check onboarding, any blockers, and then plan the canary run — I called this the "boarding pass" check so we know everyone's got a seat on the flight.
00:12 Alicia: thanks jordan, appreciate that. quick context — last week we provisioned the staging cluster, we pushed the service account but we hit that routing thing with egress. devon, can you run through?
00:23 Devon: yeah so initial egress was blocked by our firewall rules — we had only whitelisted the internal corp endpoints and forgot the probe IP range you provided. once we opened 10.2.5.0/28 it started to talk, but we saw intermittent reconnects during long generation streams.
00:40 Maya: that matches a small TCP RST we've seen on our side when the KV cache warmup overlaps with client re-connects. might be a keepalive timeout on the kube-proxy, or NAT mapping expiry.
00:55 Tom: just to be clear, this is only in staging right? prod hasn't been touched.
01:00 Devon: correct, staging only.
01:05 Jordan: good. okay so action item: devon to validate NAT timeouts and report; redwood will add a small client-side reconnect backoff in the sample client and a note in the runbook.
01:18 Alicia: on the security front, we're still waiting on SAML metadata and the KMS contact from your side — we need that for our SOC2 prep.
01:26 Maya: we can send an initial SAML assertion example and key rotation notes today; full metadata by Monday. also, KMS integration: do you plan to use your own HSM or Brightleaf's?
01:37 Alicia: we want to use our KMS (AWS KMS) and bring your runtime into our key policy, so keys never leave our account.
01:45 Maya: that's fine — we support customer KMS with envelope encryption. we'll include KMS integration steps in the playbook and a sample terraform snippet.
01:52 Tom: latency numbers — we ran the small benchmark you asked for, single-stream ~60 tokens. numbers varied: p50 92ms, p95 410ms, p99 940ms which surprised us.
02:10 Jordan: thanks tom. can you confirm model variant and sequence length?
02:13 Tom: using open-ggml/llama-compat (we called it internal-lite), seq=128, model quantized to int4.
02:21 Maya: two quick thoughts: 1) quant-to-int4 with that kernel can create P99 spikes if kernel is falling back to slower path for some layers, 2) prefix caching isn't primed in your harness, so the first in a batch steeply heavier.
02:36 Devon: and our batch script tried to micro-batch 4 by default, maybe that interacts with the quant path.
02:42 Maya: exactly — small micro-batch + int4 may trigger a slow path. our suggestion: run the experiment with fixed batch=1 and one with batch=8, and compare. also try a quant-profile that leaves the attention heads in int8 for a sanity run.
03:00 Jordan: we'll send the quant profile recommendations — maya will attach the sample docker image with both profiles.
03:07 Alicia: great. also we need observability — can you confirm what telemetry you collect by default? devon is concerned about PII.
03:14 Maya: default telemetry is token-level latency aggregated, exception counts, and optional minimal trace IDs. no request text is retained in our core telemetry; full request/response logging is opt-in and we keep it encrypted behind customer keys if enabled.
03:29 Alicia: ok that's acceptable — just add a note in the security doc.
03:33 Tom: coming back to the weird p99 — we also saw one crash that looked like OOM in the early runs.
03:40 Maya: can you paste the container OOM logs to the sheet? likely either memory fragmentation with int4 kernels or an aggressive prefetch limit. we have a patch for the prefetch in our edge build — can test in staging.
03:52 Devon: we can try that. what's the upgrade path? do we need a redeploy or can we hot-swap the runtime?
03:58 Maya: needs a rolling restart of the pod; we can do a canary redeploy with 10% for 30 minutes and monitor.
04:06 Jordan: sounds like plan. proposal: canary on 2026-08-20 16:00 UTC for 60 minutes, ramp to 100% if no errors. agree?
04:14 Alicia: yes, tentatively. devon will confirm window after checking change freeze calendar.
04:19 Tom: for the canary, what traffic profile should we run?
04:22 Maya: let's run two profiles: A) 1k small requests (seq 64, batch1) to test steady latency B) 200 mixed-length streaming requests to validate KV cache warmups. we'll provide the k6 script.
04:36 Jordan: pricing/tiers question — Alicia earlier asked about dedicated vs hosted; any recommendation for Brightleaf?
04:42 Maya: if you need consistent multi-tenant noisy neighbor guarantees and high throughput, Dedicated (reserved) is better; for early pilot hosted is faster to iterate on. given your compliance needs and expected bursty load, hybrid model (start hosted, reserve dedicated pool before prod) is common.
04:59 Alicia: ok let's capture that nuance in the proposal.
05:03 Jordan: final check — docs handoff timeline: we will send SOC2 checklist, SAML sample, KMS integration snippet, quant profiles, and the canary runbook. all by Monday 2026-08-16.
05:16 Devon: noted.
05:18 Alicia: any blockers from Redwood side?
05:21 Maya: nothing blocker-level — we'll attach the patched runtime image and instructions; one ask: can you enable enhanced verbosity for a 1-hour window during canary so we can capture traces if something odd happens?
05:33 Alicia: yes we can enable it for canary window.
05:36 Jordan: perfect. recap of action items in chat, and I'll follow up in CRM with the benchmark sheet link and the runbook. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Recap (auto):
- Outstanding network egress/NAT timeout investigation (Devon).
- Redwood to provide quant profiles, patched runtime image, and SAML/KMS snippets by 2026-08-16.
- Schedule canary 2026-08-20 pending change freeze clearance.
